implemented_requirements.requirement: Three difficulty levels (Beginner, Intermediate, Expert) with appropriate board sizes and mine counts
implemented_requirements.evidence: board.py defines DIFFICULTIES = {"Beginner": (9, 9, 10), "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40), "Expert": (16, 30, 99)} and gui.py reads the selected difficulty via DIFFICULTIES[self.diff_var.get()] to create the board.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py binds left‑click with b.bind("<Button-1>", lambda _e, r=r, c=c: self.click(r, c)) which calls Board.reveal(r, c).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.place_mines computes cell.adjacent; gui.py in refresh() sets b.config(text=str(cell.adjacent) if cell.adjacent else "") for revealed non‑mine cells.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine ends the game with a loss
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.reveal sets self.game_over = True and returns when cur.mine is True; gui.py shows a bomb emoji (MINE) and calls end_game() when board.game_over.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board display updates after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py calls self.refresh() after every click or flag action, updating button relief, text, colors, and mine counter.
gui.py binds right‑click / middle‑click / Ctrl‑click to self.flag(r, c) which calls Board.toggle_flag; Board.toggle_flag flips cell.flagged when not revealed.
gui.py in refresh() displays FLAG ("\U0001F6A9") with a gold background (bg="#FFD700") for flagged cells.

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, classic Minesweeper game with three difficulty levels, click‑to‑reveal logic, adjacency numbers, loss on mine, automatic board updates, and a functional flagging system with a unique visual. The code is self‑contained, uses only the Python standard library (Tkinter), and appears ready to run, satisfying all core benchmark requirements.
